name: Irish republicanism
summary: Irish republicanism seeks a sovereign, independent, democratic Irish republic, free of British rule and of the monarchy, and traditionally a single state for the whole island. It descends from Wolfe Tone and the United Irishmen's aim of uniting Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter, and the 1916 Proclamation guaranteeing equal rights to all. It has combined armed struggle and electoral politics, and ranges from nationalist to socialist strands.
scope: Irish republicanism as the movement's own founding texts state it: Tone's aims (independence from England; one Irish name for Protestant, Catholic and Dissenter), the 1916 Proclamation and Pearse's The Sovereign People, with an Irish Story overview of 1798 and a scholarly article on Young Ireland and the Fenians as the defining references. Modern Sinn Féin policy, dissident and legitimist strands and the Good Friday Agreement era are not covered: their sources were blocked or paywalled (sinnfein.ie, dib.ie, UCD repository, tandfonline), so those positions are left null.
